title: Dockerfile for a Node service: multi stage, non root, pinned base
when: The user wants to package a Node HTTP service or worker as a container image that is small, reproducible and does not run as root.
prompt:
Goal: A two stage Dockerfile that installs from the lockfile, copies only runtime files and runs as an unprivileged user on a pinned base.
Steps:
1. Stage build: FROM node:22.11.0-bookworm-slim AS build; WORKDIR /app; COPY package.json and the lockfile, then run the package manager's clean install, so this layer stays cached until dependencies change.
2. COPY the source, run the build script if any, then drop dev dependencies with the production only install.
3. Stage run: FROM the same exact tag (or a digest @sha256:...); ENV NODE_ENV=production; WORKDIR /app.
4. COPY --from=build --chown=node:node only node_modules, dist (or src) and package.json.
5. USER node (the official base ships it, uid 1000); EXPOSE 3000.
6. CMD ["node", "dist/server.js"] in exec form so node is PID 1 and receives SIGTERM.
7. The server reads PORT from the environment and listens on 0.0.0.0.
Quality bar:
- The final image holds no compilers, tests or .git.
- A source edit rebuilds without reinstalling dependencies.
- Every FROM names an exact version.
Pitfalls:
- FROM node:latest or a bare major, so builds change silently.
- CMD as a shell string or a package manager start script, which swallows SIGTERM.
- Listening on 127.0.0.1 inside the container, unreachable from the host.
- Copying .env or keys into a layer; they stay in the image history.
Verify:
- [ ] Two FROM lines with exact tags.
- [ ] A non root USER before CMD.
- [ ] CMD in JSON array form.
- [ ] Manifests copied before the source.
Output: Dockerfile at the project root plus a .dockerignore.

examples.input: preciso de um Dockerfile para minha API em Node na porta 3000
examples.output: two stage Dockerfile on node:22.11.0-bookworm-slim, lockfile install cached, USER node, CMD ["node", "dist/server.js"]
